messages.subject: Interpreting the car and sdcar correlation structure
parts:
My  question is about the interpretation of the car and sdcar correlation structure. I have no idea how to interpret those:


Group-Level Effects: 
~LGA (Number of levels: 16) 
              Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Eff.Sample Rhat
sd(Intercept)     0.05      0.02     0.02     0.09       5073 1.00

Correlation Structure: car(mat, ~1, 'escar')
      Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Eff.Sample Rhat
car       0.98      0.02     0.92     1.00       1555 1.01
sdcar     0.17      0.01     0.15     0.18       7289 1.00


Can somebody help?

Thank you

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Interpreting the car and sdcar correlation structure
parts:
car is the spatial autocorrelation parameter (the association between adjacent locations so to speak) and sdcar is the standard deviation of the locations (i.e. how much the locations differ with respect to the response variable). More details can also be found for instance in

Jin, Xiaoping, Bradley P. Carlin, and Sudipto Banerjee. "Generalized hierarchical multivariate CAR models for areal data." Biometrics 61.4 (2005): 950-961.
